MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron has no clear semantic selectivity — it fires weakly and diffusely across ordinary function/filler tokens in mid-sentence prose (determiners/possessives like "the", "his", auxiliaries like "be", year digits, sentence-ending ".\n"), and the very same tokens ("the", etc.) also produce its strongest negative activations, so its peaks look like generic high-frequency-token noise rather than a specific feature.

This neuron has no clean lexical trigger — it fires diffusely on tokens continuing ordinary, grammatical narrative prose (e.g. the verb after "has previously", "at least", a sentence-final period+newline, a numeral in a news figure), and is strongly *suppressed* on tokens inside repetitive, keyword-stuffed/templated boilerplate (SEO gallery titles, resume-template phrase strings, hex-color "R: G: B:" lists), so it effectively signals fluent-prose vs. list/template context.

This neuron has no clean semantic tuning — it fires at low-to-moderate strength on the token that opens an upcoming content phrase mid-clause (a determiner, pronoun, quantifier, verb, or the first sub-word of a compound noun, e.g. " a"/" I"/" most"/" pay"/" Pe"acemaker) and is suppressed on clause-final commas/periods, so it looks like a noisy "start of a new phrase after a verb/copula" detector rather than a concept detector.
